byProvider.description: Per-agent provider-specific tool policy overrides for channel-scoped capability control. Use this when a single agent needs tighter restrictions on one provider than others.

codeMode.title: Agent Code Mode
codeMode.description: Per-agent Code Mode options. Explicit enabled overrides the shared model and global activation defaults; an agent-specific model codeMode override wins. Other options merge over tools.codeMode without changing activation.

swarm.title: Agent Swarm
swarm.description: Per-agent swarm override. Values merge over the top-level tools.swarm configuration.

allowInSandbox.title: Allow Agent GitHub Identity in Sandbox
allowInSandbox.description: Allows this agent's managed GitHub credentials and Git author inside its own Docker or Podman sandbox (default: false). Shared scope refuses identity injection; other backends reject provisioning. Security audit warns while enabled.

github.title: Agent GitHub CLI Identity Override
github.description: Complete managed GitHub CLI identity and Git author override for this agent. Omit it to inherit the system identity.

send.title: Agent Send Destination Allowlist
send.description: Agent ids or * patterns this agent may contact with sessions_send, even with narrow tools.sessions.visibility. Omitted inherits visibility; [] denies ordinary cross-agent sends. Global tools.agentToAgent and sandbox limits still apply. Does not grant list, history, search, status, or watch access; replies belong only to the sent turn. Requester-owned child session access is unchanged.

agentToAgent.title: Agent Outbound Messaging
agentToAgent.description: Outbound-only agent messaging policy. Explicit send destinations do not grant session reads or status access, and remain bounded by global agent-to-agent participation and sandbox restrictions.

allowWithinProvider.title: Agent Cross-Context Messaging (Same Provider)
allowWithinProvider.description: Per-agent message guard for sending to other conversations on the same provider. Set both this and allowAcrossProviders to false for current-conversation-only public agents.

allowAcrossProviders.title: Agent Cross-Context Messaging (Across Providers)
allowAcrossProviders.description: Per-agent override for sending across providers. Inherits the global setting (default: true). Set false to block cross-provider messaging for this agent.

allow.title: Agent Message Action Allowlist
allow.description: Per-agent message action allowlist for the message tool. Set to a minimal list such as ["send"] for public sandbox agents so read, edit, delete, reaction, and other provider-specific message actions stay hidden and blocked.

entries.title: Agent List
entries.description: Explicit list of configured agents with IDs and optional overrides for model, tools, identity, and workspace. Keep IDs stable over time so bindings, approvals, and session routing remain deterministic.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Agent runtime configuration root. Root siblings own infrastructure and cross-agent defaults; agents.defaults owns agent-loop behavior; agent entries may override either where supported.

worktreeRoot.title: Worktree Root
worktreeRoot.description: Global directory for new managed worktrees. Use an absolute path or ~ for your home directory; defaults to <state-dir>/worktrees. Existing worktrees keep their recorded paths when this changes.

worktreeAcceleration.title: Worktree Acceleration
worktreeAcceleration.description: Use filesystem acceleration for new managed worktrees when supported (default: true). Set false to use normal Git checkout and file copying. Applies only to new worktrees.

worktreeMaxCount.title: Maximum Managed Worktrees
worktreeMaxCount.description: Maximum live managed worktrees across all agents and repositories (default: 4096). Evicts merged or squashed branches first, then oldest idle worktrees, including unsaved data. Live runs are protected; raise this value if they occupy the cap. Disk-space admission still applies.

profile.title: Tool Profile
profile.description: Global tool profile name used to select a predefined tool policy baseline before applying allow/deny overrides. Use this for consistent environment posture across agents and keep profile names stable.

allow.title: Tool Allowlist
allow.description: Absolute tool allowlist that replaces profile-derived defaults for strict environments. Use this only when you intentionally run a tightly curated subset of tool capabilities.

alsoAllow.title: Tool Allowlist Additions
alsoAllow.description: Extra tool allowlist entries merged on top of the selected tool profile and default policy. Keep this list small and explicit so audits can quickly identify intentional policy exceptions.

deny.title: Tool Denylist
deny.description: Global tool denylist that blocks listed tools even when profile or provider rules would allow them. Use deny rules for emergency lockouts and long-term defense-in-depth.

byProvider.title: Tool Policy by Provider
byProvider.description: Per-provider tool allow/deny overrides keyed by channel/provider ID to tailor capabilities by surface. Use this when one provider needs stricter controls than global tool policy.

enabled.title: Enable Web Search Tool
enabled.description: Enable managed web_search and optional Codex-native search for eligible models.

provider.title: Web Search Provider
provider.description: Search provider id. Auto-detected from available API keys if omitted.

timeoutSeconds.title: Web Search Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for web_search requests.

cacheTtlMinutes.title: Web Search Cache TTL (min)
cacheTtlMinutes.description: Cache TTL in minutes for web_search results.

enabled.title: Enable Native Codex Web Search
enabled.description: Enable native Codex web search for Codex-capable models.

mode.title: Codex Web Search Mode
mode.description: Native Codex web search preference: "cached" (default; unrestricted Codex turns resolve it to live) or "live".

allowedDomains.title: Codex Allowed Domains
allowedDomains.description: Domain allowlist for native Codex web_search. On native-hosted-search turns, it also gates managed web_fetch; managed-provider turns are unchanged.

contextSize.title: Codex Search Context Size
contextSize.description: Native Codex search context size hint: "low", "medium", or "high".

country.title: Codex User Country
country.description: Approximate country sent to native Codex web search.

region.title: Codex User Region
region.description: Approximate region/state sent to native Codex web search.

city.title: Codex User City
city.description: Approximate city sent to native Codex web search.

timezone.title: Codex User Timezone
timezone.description: Approximate timezone sent to native Codex web search.

enabled.title: Enable Web Fetch Tool
enabled.description: Enable the web_fetch tool (lightweight HTTP fetch).

maxCharsCap.title: Web Fetch Hard Max Chars
maxCharsCap.description: Hard cap for web_fetch maxChars (applies to config and tool calls).

timeoutSeconds.title: Web Fetch Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for web_fetch requests.

cacheTtlMinutes.title: Web Fetch Cache TTL (min)
cacheTtlMinutes.description: Cache TTL in minutes for web_fetch results.

userAgent.title: Web Fetch User-Agent
userAgent.description: Override User-Agent header for web_fetch requests.

headers.title: Web Fetch Request Headers
headers.description: Extra request headers sent with direct web_fetch requests, for example gateway routing or authentication headers. Every configured value is treated as sensitive and redacted from exposed config and debug captures. Values are plain strings, support ${VAR} substitution and the global $${VAR} literal escape, and are sent to model-chosen URLs. Entries are validated when the request is built rather than at config load, so a bad name or unsendable value is dropped and logged instead of disabling the surface; Accept, Accept-Language, User-Agent, and framing headers such as Transfer-Encoding are dropped too. Use tools.web.fetch.userAgent to change the user agent. Cross-origin redirects retain only the guarded-fetch safe header allowlist, and changing the headers actually sent partitions the fetch cache.

readability.title: Web Fetch Readability Extraction
readability.description: Use Readability to extract main content from HTML (fallbacks to basic HTML cleanup).

useTrustedEnvProxy.title: Web Fetch Trusted Env Proxy
useTrustedEnvProxy.description: Route web_fetch through a trusted HTTP(S) env proxy and let the proxy resolve DNS. Enable only when that proxy is operator-controlled and enforces outbound policy after DNS resolution.

dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.title: Web Fetch Dangerously Allow Private Network
dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.description: Allows web_fetch access to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless model-selected URLs are trusted in this deployment.

allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange.title: Web Fetch Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange.description: Allow RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15) for fake-IP proxy compatibility such as Clash or Surge.

allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange.title: Web Fetch Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange.description: Allow IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7) for trusted fake-IP proxy compatibility such as sing-box, Clash, or Surge.

allowedHostnames.title: Web Fetch Allowed Hostnames
allowedHostnames.description: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for web_fetch, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

blockedHostnames.title: Web Fetch Blocked Hostnames
blockedHostnames.description: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules on every web_fetch redirect. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

ssrfPolicy.title: Web Fetch SSRF Policy
ssrfPolicy.description: Scoped SSRF policy overrides for web_fetch. Keep this narrow and opt in only for known local-network proxy environments.

web.title: Web Tools
web.description: Web-tool policy grouping for search/fetch providers, limits, and fallback behavior tuning. Keep enabled settings aligned with API key availability and outbound networking policy.

profileId.title: GitHub Profile Version
profileId.description: Opaque generated profile version used to switch managed credentials atomically.

kind.title: GitHub Credential Kind
kind.description: Marks a managed OAuth profile whose rotating refresh credential is owned by the Gateway. Omitted profiles use a personal access token.

name.title: Git Author Name
name.description: Optional process-local Git author and committer name.

email.title: Git Author Email
email.description: Optional process-local Git author and committer email.

github.title: GitHub CLI Identity and Git Author
github.description: Managed local GitHub CLI profile and optional Git author for agent tools. Omit this object to preserve the Gateway runtime user's native account and author; repository remote credentials are never overridden.

models.title: Media Understanding Shared Models
models.description: Canonical media-understanding model list. Use image, audio, or video capability tags on every entry so each pipeline selects only compatible fallbacks.

concurrency.title: Media Understanding Concurrency
concurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent media understanding operations per turn across image, audio, and video tasks. Lower this in resource-constrained deployments to prevent CPU/network saturation.

enabled.title: Enable Image Understanding
enabled.description: Enable image understanding so attached or referenced images can be interpreted into textual context. Disable if you need text-only operation or want to avoid image-processing cost.

preferredModel.title: Preferred Image Understanding Model
preferredModel.description: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for image understanding before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

scope.title: Image Understanding Scope
scope.description: Restrict image understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow in busy or untrusted channels to control processing.

maxBytes.title: Image Understanding Max Bytes
maxBytes.description: Default image input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to match provider payload limits and deployment bandwidth.

maxChars.title: Image Understanding Max Chars
maxChars.description: Default maximum image description length. Use a lower value for compact context or a higher value for detailed OCR and scene analysis.

prompt.title: Image Understanding Prompt
prompt.description: Default image-understanding prompt when an entry does not override it. Keep this deterministic when consumers rely on stable descriptions.

timeoutSeconds.title: Image Understanding Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Default timeout for image-understanding requests. Increase it for large images or slower local vision models.

attachments.title: Image Understanding Attachment Policy
attachments.description: Choose which matching image attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-image analysis is intentional.

enabled.title: Enable Audio Understanding
enabled.description: Enable audio understanding so voice notes or audio clips can be transcribed for agent context.

preferredModel.title: Preferred Audio Understanding Model
preferredModel.description: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for audio transcription before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

scope.title: Audio Understanding Scope
scope.description: Restrict audio understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow where automatic transcription is sensitive or expensive.

maxBytes.title: Audio Understanding Max Bytes
maxBytes.description: Default audio input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to the largest recording your providers and network should accept.

maxChars.title: Audio Understanding Max Chars
maxChars.description: Default maximum transcript length for configured and auto-detected models. Use a lower value to keep long voice notes from expanding agent context.

prompt.title: Audio Understanding Prompt
prompt.description: Default audio transcription prompt when a model entry does not override it. Keep the instruction stable when downstream workflows rely on transcript style.

timeoutSeconds.title: Audio Understanding Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Default timeout for audio understanding requests. Increase it for long recordings or slower local transcription models.

language.title: Audio Understanding Language
language.description: Default language hint for audio transcription providers. Set it when the primary spoken language is known and provider detection is unreliable.

attachments.title: Audio Understanding Attachment Policy
attachments.description: Choose which matching audio attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-attachment transcription is intentional.

echoTranscript.title: Echo Transcript to Chat
echoTranscript.description: Echo the audio transcript to the originating chat before agent processing. Enable this when users need to verify what the system heard.

echoFormat.title: Transcript Echo Format
echoFormat.description: Format the echoed transcript with a {transcript} placeholder. Keep the placeholder intact so delivery includes the transcript.

enabled.title: Enable Video Understanding
enabled.description: Enable video understanding so clips can be summarized into text for downstream reasoning and responses. Disable when processing video is out of policy or too expensive for your deployment.

preferredModel.title: Preferred Video Understanding Model
preferredModel.description: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for video understanding before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

scope.title: Video Understanding Scope
scope.description: Restrict video understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow in busy or untrusted channels to control processing.

maxBytes.title: Video Understanding Max Bytes
maxBytes.description: Default video input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to match provider payload limits and deployment bandwidth.

maxChars.title: Video Understanding Max Chars
maxChars.description: Default maximum video description length. Use a lower value for compact context or a higher value for detailed scene summaries.

prompt.title: Video Understanding Prompt
prompt.description: Default video-understanding prompt when an entry does not override it. Keep this deterministic when consumers rely on stable summaries.

timeoutSeconds.title: Video Understanding Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Default timeout for video-understanding requests. Increase it for longer clips or slower local analysis models.

attachments.title: Video Understanding Attachment Policy
attachments.description: Choose which matching video attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-video analysis is intentional.

enabled.title: Enable Link Understanding
enabled.description: Enable automatic link understanding pre-processing so URLs can be summarized before agent reasoning. Keep enabled for richer context, and disable when strict minimal processing is required.

scope.title: Link Understanding Scope
scope.description: Controls when link understanding runs relative to conversation context and message type. Keep scope conservative to avoid unnecessary fetches on messages where links are not actionable.

maxLinks.title: Link Understanding Max Links
maxLinks.description: Maximum number of links expanded per turn during link understanding. Use lower values to control latency/cost in chatty threads and higher values when multi-link context is critical.

timeoutSeconds.title: Link Understanding Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Per-link understanding timeout budget in seconds before unresolved links are skipped. Keep this bounded to avoid long stalls when external sites are slow or unreachable.

models.title: Link Understanding Models
models.description: Preferred model list for link understanding tasks, evaluated in order as fallbacks when supported. Use lightweight models first for routine summarization and heavier models only when needed.

visibility.title: Session Tools Visibility
visibility.description: Controls which sessions can be targeted by sessions_list/sessions_history/sessions_search/sessions_send/session_status. ("all" default = any session on the Gateway, including other agents and users; "agent" = any session in the current agent id; "self" = only current; "tree" = current session + spawned subagent sessions). Cross-agent access is on by default and scoped by tools.agentToAgent; use narrower visibility to restrict reads and ordinary sends. Explicit agents.entries.<id>.tools.agentToAgent.send destinations can permit sends without widening reads.

enabled.title: Tool-loop Detection
enabled.description: Controls rolling-history tool-loop detection and the post-compaction guard. Omit to keep rolling detection off and post-compaction protection on. Set true to enable both, or false to disable both.

enabled.title: Enable Tool Search
enabled.description: Enables Tool Search. When on, OpenClaw hides large tool catalogs behind structured search/describe/call tools during embedded runtime runs.

mode.title: Tool Search Surface
mode.description: Choose the model-facing surface: "tools" (default) exposes structured search/describe/call tools; "directory" keeps a bounded tool directory visible, exposes a bounded set of likely or required schemas, and defers the rest behind search/describe/call.

searchDefaultLimit.title: Tool Search Default Results
searchDefaultLimit.description: Default number of Tool Search results returned when the model omits a limit. Runtime clamps this to `maxSearchLimit`.

maxSearchLimit.title: Tool Search Max Results
maxSearchLimit.description: Maximum number of Tool Search results a model can request. Runtime clamps values to the supported 1..50 range.

toolSearch.title: Tool Search
toolSearch.description: Compact large OpenClaw, MCP, and client tool catalogs. OpenClaw runtimes use structured Tool Search automatically when unset; engaged Code Mode takes precedence and Codex uses its native search. Set false to disable it, true for structured search, or use the object form to choose a mode.

enabled.title: Enable Code Mode
enabled.description: Global OpenClaw Code Mode activation. A completely absent global setting defaults to `"auto"`; an authored object without `enabled` remains off. `"auto"` engages catalog-preferred models, while `true` engages tool-capable runs. Agent and model activation overrides take precedence. An engaged run fails closed if the runtime is unavailable instead of exposing the full tool list.

executor.title: Code Mode Executor
executor.description: JavaScript executor: "node" (default) uses Node vm for trusted code and is not a security sandbox; "quickjs" uses the bundled QuickJS WASM plugin for hardened guest execution. Tool permissions apply to both. A missing selected executor fails closed.

mode.title: Code Mode Surface
mode.description: Model-facing surface. Only "only" is supported: expose code-mode `exec` and `wait` and hide normal tools.

timeoutMs.title: Code Mode Timeout
timeoutMs.description: Maximum milliseconds for one code-mode `exec` or `wait` call.

memoryLimitBytes.title: Code Mode Memory Limit
memoryLimitBytes.description: QuickJS guest heap limit or best-effort Node worker V8 heap budget in bytes. Node runtime overhead and minimum engine allocations affect the effective budget; external buffers and process RSS are excluded. This is not a security guarantee.

maxOutputBytes.title: Code Mode Output Limit
maxOutputBytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes returned through code-mode output.

maxSnapshotBytes.title: Code Mode Snapshot Limit
maxSnapshotBytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes retained for one suspended QuickJS snapshot.

maxPendingToolCalls.title: Code Mode Pending Tool Limit
maxPendingToolCalls.description: Maximum concurrent nested tool calls a code-mode VM can start before it must resume later.

snapshotTtlSeconds.title: Code Mode Snapshot TTL
snapshotTtlSeconds.description: How long suspended Code Mode runs can be resumed with `wait` before they expire.

searchDefaultLimit.title: Code Mode Default Search Results
searchDefaultLimit.description: Default number of hidden catalog search results returned by `catalog.search` inside code mode.

maxSearchLimit.title: Code Mode Max Search Results
maxSearchLimit.description: Maximum number of hidden catalog search results a code-mode program can request.

codeMode.title: Code Mode
codeMode.description: Generic OpenClaw Code Mode. When omitted globally, defaults to `"auto"`; an authored object without `enabled` remains off. Engaged agent runs expose only `exec` and `wait` to the model and access normal tools through the catalog bridge.

enabled.title: Enable Swarm
enabled.description: Enables collector-mode subagents and agents_wait. Default is on; set false to opt out.

maxConcurrent.title: Swarm Concurrent Children per Group
maxConcurrent.description: Maximum running collector children in each swarm group's separate execution lane (default: 32), independent of ordinary subagent concurrency. Each running child uses one model stream and one Code Mode worker isolate. Group admission limits still apply.

maxChildrenPerGroup.title: Swarm Live Children per Group
maxChildrenPerGroup.description: Maximum live collector children per swarm group.

maxTotalPerGroup.title: Swarm Total Children per Group
maxTotalPerGroup.description: Maximum lifetime collector spawns per swarm group.

waitTimeoutSecondsMax.title: Swarm Maximum Wait Timeout
waitTimeoutSecondsMax.description: Maximum timeout accepted by agents_wait, in seconds.

defaultAgentId.title: Swarm Default Agent
defaultAgentId.description: Default target agent for swarm spawns that omit agentId. The subagent allowlist still applies.

swarm.title: Swarm
swarm.description: Collector-mode subagent orchestration. Enabled by default; set false to opt out. Tool permissions still apply to agents_wait and swarm spawn options.

allowWithinProvider.title: Allow Cross-Context (Same Provider)
allowWithinProvider.description: Allow sends to other channels within the same provider (default: true).

allowAcrossProviders.title: Allow Cross-Context (Across Providers)
allowAcrossProviders.description: Allow sends across different providers (default: true). Set false to block cross-provider messaging.

enabled.title: Cross-Context Marker
enabled.description: Add a visible origin marker when sending cross-context (default: true).

allow.title: Message Action Allowlist
allow.description: Global message action allowlist for the message tool. Use only when the whole runtime should expose and accept a reduced action set; prefer per-agent allowlists for public or sandboxed agents.

enabled.title: Enable Message Broadcast
enabled.description: Enable broadcast action (default: true).

enabled.title: Enable Agent-to-Agent Tool
enabled.description: Enables cross-agent session tool access (default: true); omitted or empty allow permits every agent pair. Set false to block ordinary cross-agent access; requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under tree or all visibility. For strict separation, set tools.sessions.visibility to agent or self (tree still admits requester-owned native/ACP children), or use separate gateways.

allow.title: Agent-to-Agent Target Allowlist
allow.description: Agent ids or * patterns that may take part in cross-agent calls; the requesting and target agent must both match. Cross-agent access is on by default, and omitted or empty allow permits every pair. Set an explicit list to restrict access; blank entries deny.

agentToAgent.title: Agent-to-Agent Tool Access
agentToAgent.description: Policy for cross-agent session tool calls: sends, list, history, search, and status reads (default: enabled). Use allow to restrict agent pairs; enabled=false blocks ordinary cross-agent access. Requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under tree or all visibility. For strict separation, set tools.sessions.visibility to agent or self (tree still admits requester-owned native/ACP children), or use separate gateways.

enabled.title: Enable Elevated Tool Access
enabled.description: Enables elevated tool execution path when sender and policy checks pass. Keep disabled in public/shared channels and enable only for trusted owner-operated contexts.

allowFrom.title: Elevated Tool Allow Rules
allowFrom.description: Sender allow rules for elevated tools, usually keyed by channel/provider identity formats. Use narrow, explicit identities so elevated commands cannot be triggered by unintended users.

elevated.title: Elevated Tool Access
elevated.description: Elevated tool access controls for privileged command surfaces that should only be reachable from trusted senders. Keep disabled unless operator workflows explicitly require elevated actions.

host.title: Exec Target
host.description: Selects execution target strategy for shell commands. Use "auto" for runtime-aware behavior (sandbox when available, otherwise gateway), or pin sandbox/gateway/node explicitly when you need a fixed surface.

mode.title: Exec Mode
mode.description: Normalized exec policy selector. Use "auto" for classifier-reviewed approval misses, "ask" for human-reviewed misses, "allowlist" for deterministic safe commands only, or "full" for trusted local operation.

node.title: Exec Node Binding
node.description: Node binding configuration for exec tooling when command execution is delegated through connected nodes. Use explicit node binding only when multi-node routing is required.

pathPrepend.title: Exec PATH Prepend
pathPrepend.description: Directories to prepend to PATH for exec runs (gateway/sandbox).

safeBins.title: Exec Safe Bins
safeBins.description: Allow stdin-only safe binaries to run without explicit allowlist entries.

strictInlineEval.title: Require Inline-Eval Approval
strictInlineEval.description: Require explicit approval for interpreter inline-eval forms such as `python -c`, `node -e`, `ruby -e`, or `osascript -e`. Prevents silent allowlist reuse and downgrades allow-always to ask-each-time for those forms.

commandHighlighting.title: Exec Command Highlighting
commandHighlighting.description: Show parser-derived command highlights in exec approval prompts (default: false). Enable this to render highlighted command text without changing exec approval policy.

grantExpiryDays.title: Standing Grant Expiry (Days)
grantExpiryDays.description: Default lifetime, in days (1-3650), for standing grants minted by allow-always on automation approvals. Unset keeps grants valid until revoked or the owning automation changes. Terms freeze at mint, so changing this affects only future grants.

safeBinTrustedDirs.title: Exec Safe Bin Trusted Dirs
safeBinTrustedDirs.description: Additional explicit directories trusted for safe-bin path checks (PATH entries are never auto-trusted).

safeBinProfiles.title: Exec Safe Bin Profiles
safeBinProfiles.description: Optional per-binary safe-bin profiles (positional limits + allowed/denied flags).

model.title: Exec Reviewer Model
model.description: Optional provider/model override for the exec reviewer agent. Omit to reuse the configured primary model for the target agent.

thinking.title: Exec Reviewer Thinking
thinking.description: Optional reasoning effort for OpenClaw model-backed approval reviews: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max. Omit to preserve provider defaults. Supported levels are normalized for the selected model. Does not configure native Codex Guardian.

fastMode.title: Exec Reviewer Fast Mode
fastMode.description: Optional Fast mode for OpenClaw approval reviews: true requests priority processing on supported OpenAI Responses and ChatGPT/OAuth routes; false requests standard processing. Omit to preserve provider defaults. Fast mode may cost more and is subject to provider availability. Does not configure native Codex Guardian.

timeoutMs.title: Exec Reviewer Timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.description: Per-stage exec reviewer timeout in milliseconds for model preparation and completion before falling back to human approval (default: 30000).

reviewer.title: Exec Reviewer
reviewer.description: Model-backed exec reviewer used by auto mode before human approval fallback. Configure a narrow model override here when you want exec review isolated from the main agent model.

approvalRunningNoticeMs.title: Exec Approval Running Notice (ms)
approvalRunningNoticeMs.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing an in-progress notice after an exec approval is granted. Increase to reduce flicker for fast commands, or lower for quicker operator feedback.

notifyOnExit.title: Exec Notify On Exit
notifyOnExit.description: When true (default), backgrounded exec sessions on exit and node exec lifecycle events enqueue a system event and request a heartbeat.

notifyOnExitEmptySuccess.title: Exec Notify On Empty Success
notifyOnExitEmptySuccess.description: When true, successful backgrounded exec exits with empty output still enqueue a completion system event (default: false).

enabled.title: Enable apply_patch
enabled.description: Enable or disable apply_patch for OpenAI and OpenAI Codex models when allowed by tool policy (default: true).

workspaceOnly.title: apply_patch Workspace-Only
workspaceOnly.description: Restrict apply_patch paths to the workspace directory (default: true). Set false to allow writing outside the workspace (dangerous).

allowModels.title: apply_patch Model Allowlist
allowModels.description: Optional allowlist of model ids (e.g. "gpt-5.4" or "openai/gpt-5.4").

exec.title: Exec Tool
exec.description: Exec-tool policy grouping for shell execution host, security mode, approval behavior, and runtime bindings. Keep conservative defaults in production and tighten elevated execution paths.

workspaceOnly.title: Workspace-only FS tools
workspaceOnly.description: Restrict filesystem tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch) to the workspace directory (default: false).

tools.title: Subagent Tool Allow/Deny Policy
tools.description: Allow/deny tool policy applied to spawned subagent runtimes. Keep this narrower than parent scope. Parent-owned tools such as progress_card are always denied, including through allow/alsoAllow.

subagents.title: Subagent Tool Policy
subagents.description: Tool policy wrapper for spawned subagents to restrict or expand tool availability compared to parent defaults. Use this to keep delegated agent capabilities scoped to task intent.

tools.title: Sandbox Tool Allow/Deny Policy
tools.description: Allow/deny tool policy applied when agents run in sandboxed execution environments. Keep policies minimal so sandbox tasks cannot escalate into unnecessary external actions.

sandbox.title: Sandbox Tool Policy
sandbox.description: Tool policy wrapper for sandboxed agent executions so sandbox runs can have distinct capability boundaries. Use this to enforce stronger safety in sandbox contexts.

updatePlan.title: Enable Structured Plan Tool
updatePlan.description: Unified `progress_card` status tool for durable plans and narrative notes in parent sessions. Enabled by default; set false to opt out. Always unavailable to subagents.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Tool infrastructure and cross-agent defaults. Root siblings own infrastructure and cross-agent defaults; agents.defaults owns agent-loop behavior; agent entries may override either where supported.

type.title: Binding Type
type.description: Binding kind. Use "route" (or omit for legacy route entries) for normal routing, and "acp" for persistent ACP conversation bindings.

agentId.title: Binding Agent ID
agentId.description: Target agent ID that receives traffic when the corresponding binding match rule is satisfied. Use valid configured agent IDs only so routing does not fail at runtime.

channel.title: Binding Channel
channel.description: Channel/provider identifier this binding applies to, such as `telegram`, `discord`, or a plugin channel ID. Use the configured channel key exactly so binding evaluation works reliably.

accountId.title: Binding Account ID
accountId.description: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups so the binding applies only to one identity. Use this when account scoping is required for the route and leave unset otherwise.

kind.title: Binding Peer Kind
kind.description: Peer conversation type: "direct", "group", "channel", or legacy "dm" (deprecated alias for direct). Prefer "direct" for new configs and keep kind aligned with channel semantics.

id.title: Binding Peer ID
id.description: Conversation identifier used with peer matching, such as a chat ID, channel ID, or group ID from the provider. Keep this exact to avoid silent non-matches.

peer.title: Binding Peer Match
peer.description: Optional peer matcher for specific conversations including peer kind and peer id. Use this when only one direct/group/channel target should be pinned to an agent.

guildId.title: Binding Guild ID
guildId.description: Optional Discord-style guild/server ID constraint for binding evaluation in multi-server deployments. Use this when the same peer identifiers can appear across different guilds.

teamId.title: Binding Team ID
teamId.description: Optional team/workspace ID constraint used by providers that scope chats under teams. Add this when you need bindings isolated to one workspace context.

roles.title: Binding Roles
roles.description: Optional role-based filter list used by providers that attach roles to chat context. Use this to route privileged or operational role traffic to specialized agents.

match.title: Binding Match Rule
match.description: Match rule object for deciding when a binding applies, including channel and optional account/peer constraints. Keep rules narrow to avoid accidental agent takeover across contexts.

dmScope.title: Binding Session DM Scope
dmScope.description: Optional DM session scope override for this route binding. For example, keep global session.dmScope="main" while using "per-account-channel-peer" for selected direct peers.

groupScope.title: Binding Session Group Scope
groupScope.description: Optional group/channel session scope override for this route binding. "per-group" keeps matched rooms separate and ambiently watched by the agent main session regardless of dmScope; "main" merges their context into main and needs no watch.

session.title: Binding Session
session.description: Optional route session overrides for conversations matched by this binding. Use this when a narrow route should keep the same agent but isolate session continuity differently.

type.title: Binding Type
type.description: Binding kind. Use "route" (or omit for legacy route entries) for normal routing, and "acp" for persistent ACP conversation bindings.

agentId.title: Binding Agent ID
agentId.description: Target agent ID that receives traffic when the corresponding binding match rule is satisfied. Use valid configured agent IDs only so routing does not fail at runtime.

channel.title: Binding Channel
channel.description: Channel/provider identifier this binding applies to, such as `telegram`, `discord`, or a plugin channel ID. Use the configured channel key exactly so binding evaluation works reliably.

accountId.title: Binding Account ID
accountId.description: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups so the binding applies only to one identity. Use this when account scoping is required for the route and leave unset otherwise.

kind.title: Binding Peer Kind
kind.description: Peer conversation type: "direct", "group", "channel", or legacy "dm" (deprecated alias for direct). Prefer "direct" for new configs and keep kind aligned with channel semantics.

id.title: Binding Peer ID
id.description: Conversation identifier used with peer matching, such as a chat ID, channel ID, or group ID from the provider. Keep this exact to avoid silent non-matches.

peer.title: Binding Peer Match
peer.description: Optional peer matcher for specific conversations including peer kind and peer id. Use this when only one direct/group/channel target should be pinned to an agent.

guildId.title: Binding Guild ID
guildId.description: Optional Discord-style guild/server ID constraint for binding evaluation in multi-server deployments. Use this when the same peer identifiers can appear across different guilds.

teamId.title: Binding Team ID
teamId.description: Optional team/workspace ID constraint used by providers that scope chats under teams. Add this when you need bindings isolated to one workspace context.

roles.title: Binding Roles
roles.description: Optional role-based filter list used by providers that attach roles to chat context. Use this to route privileged or operational role traffic to specialized agents.

match.title: Binding Match Rule
match.description: Match rule object for deciding when a binding applies, including channel and optional account/peer constraints. Keep rules narrow to avoid accidental agent takeover across contexts.

mode.title: ACP Binding Mode
mode.description: ACP session mode override for this binding (persistent or oneshot).

label.title: ACP Binding Label
label.description: Human-friendly label for ACP status/diagnostics in this bound conversation.

cwd.title: ACP Binding Working Directory
cwd.description: Working directory override for ACP sessions created from this binding.

backend.title: ACP Binding Backend
backend.description: ACP backend override for this binding (falls back to agent runtime ACP backend, then global acp.backend).

acp.title: ACP Binding Overrides
acp.description: Optional per-binding ACP overrides for bindings[].type=acp. This layer overrides agents.entries.*.runtime.acp defaults for the matched conversation.

bindings.title: Bindings
bindings.description: Top-level binding rules for routing and persistent ACP conversation ownership. Use type=route for normal routing and type=acp for persistent ACP harness bindings.

strategy.title: Agent Group Strategy
strategy.description: Participant execution order: "parallel" (default) runs agents concurrently, while "sequential" runs them in configured order. Each round completes before the next begins.

agents.title: Agent Group Participants
agents.description: Participant agent IDs from agents.entries (maximum: 16). Each participant uses its own session for this channel, account, conversation, and thread.

mentionGating.title: Agent Group Mention Selection
mentionGating.description: Select only explicitly @mentioned participants when any match; otherwise run all participants (default: true). Bare names or emoji do not select participants. Channel allowlists and admission rules still apply.

maxRounds.title: Agent Group Maximum Rounds
maxRounds.description: Maximum rounds per inbound message, including the initial round (integer: 1–4, default: 1). Follow-up rounds share bounded, attributed sibling replies and stop when every participant passes.

maxTurns.title: Agent Group Maximum Turns
maxTurns.description: Maximum participant turns per inbound message across all rounds (integer: 1–32, default: agents.length). Slots are reserved before parallel dispatch; this bounds agent turns, not physical message chunks or tool sends. Budgets do not resume after restart.

additionalProperties.title: Agent Group Participants and Options
additionalProperties.description: Use a channel-qualified peer ID (for example "telegram:-100123") to configure an array of agent IDs or a strict object with agents, mentionGating, maxRounds, and maxTurns. Qualified entries take precedence over legacy WhatsApp peer keys and allow at most 16 agents.

broadcast.title: Agent Group Threads
broadcast.description: Use agent group threads to run several configured agents on one inbound conversation, each in its own session. Channel-qualified entries support bounded follow-up rounds; legacy WhatsApp peer arrays retain single-pass behavior.

ttlHours.title: Attachment Retention TTL (hours)
ttlHours.description: Optional retention window in hours for persisted media handled by the general mtime sweep. Leave unset to disable that sweep, or set values like 24 (1 day) or 168 (7 days) to periodically remove older staged media. Managed outgoing media (chat-generated attachments) is excluded and follows its own SQLite- and transcript-aware retention.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Top-level retention behavior shared across providers and tools that persist media. Use ttlHours when general staged media needs bounded cleanup.

visibleReplies.title: Visible Replies
visibleReplies.description: Controls model-authored source replies across direct, group, and channel conversations. "message_tool" requires message(action=send) for normal assistant output and generic tool media; explicitly host-owned runtime output remains deliverable except for ambient room events. "automatic" posts normal replies as before.

usageTemplate.title: Usage Footer Template
usageTemplate.description: Custom /usage full footer template, either an inline object or a JSON file path. Invalid or unavailable templates fall back to the built-in usage line.

responseUsage.title: Default Usage Footer Mode
responseUsage.description: Default per-reply usage footer mode ("off"|"tokens"|"full") seeded into sessions that have not chosen one via /usage. Also accepts "on" as a legacy alias for "tokens". Accepts a bare mode or a per-channel map with a "default" fallback. Precedence: session value -> channel entry -> default -> off; an explicit /usage choice (including off) is persisted and overrides the default. Use /usage reset (aliases: inherit, clear, default) to clear a session override and re-inherit this configured default.

mentionPatterns.title: Group Mention Patterns
mentionPatterns.description: Safe case-insensitive regex patterns used to detect explicit mentions/trigger phrases in group chats. Use precise patterns to reduce false positives in high-volume channels; invalid or unsafe nested-repetition patterns are ignored.

historyLimit.title: Group History Limit
historyLimit.description: Maximum number of prior group messages loaded as context per turn for group sessions. Use higher values for richer continuity, or lower values for faster and cheaper responses. Automatic prompt history is capped at 200 messages. The JSON integer maximum selects the channel default window (50 for shared group history), not an unlimited window.

unmentionedInbound.title: Group Unmentioned Inbound
unmentionedInbound.description: Controls how unmentioned always-on group chatter is submitted. "user_request" treats it as a user request; "room_event" submits it as quiet context where visible output requires the message tool.

visibleReplies.title: Group Visible Replies
visibleReplies.description: Overrides model-authored source replies for group/channel conversations. Defaults to "automatic" when no global visible reply policy is set. "message_tool" requires message(action=send) for normal assistant output and generic tool media; explicitly host-owned runtime output remains deliverable except for ambient room events. "automatic" posts normal replies as before.

groupChat.title: Group Chat Rules
groupChat.description: Group-message handling controls including mention triggers and history window sizing. Keep mention patterns narrow so group channels do not trigger on every message.

mode.title: Queue Mode
mode.description: Queue mode for active runs. Use "steer" to inject prompts into the active run, "followup" to run later, "collect" to batch compatible messages later, or "interrupt" to abort the active run before starting the newest prompt.

byChannel.title: Queue Mode by Channel
byChannel.description: Per-channel queue mode overrides keyed by channel ID, including plugin channels (for example discord, telegram, x). Use this when one channel's traffic pattern needs different behavior than global defaults.

debounceMsByChannel.title: Queue Fallback Debounce by Channel (ms)
debounceMsByChannel.description: Per-channel debounce overrides for queue behavior keyed by channel ID, including plugin channels. Use this to tune burst handling independently for chat surfaces with different pacing.

cap.title: Queue Capacity
cap.description: Maximum number of queued inbound items retained before drop policy applies. Default is 20; keep caps bounded in noisy channels so memory usage remains predictable.

drop.title: Queue Drop Strategy
drop.description: Drop strategy when queue cap is exceeded. "summarize" drops oldest entries but preserves compact summaries; "old" drops oldest without summaries; "new" rejects the newest item. Use "summarize" for long-running chats where context matters.

queue.title: Inbound Queue
queue.description: Queue strategy for inbound messages that arrive while a session run is active. Use this to tune steering, deferred followups, batching, or interruption.

debounceMs.title: Inbound Message Debounce (ms)
debounceMs.description: Quiet window (ms) for batching rapid inbound messages from the same sender. Telegram defaults to 300ms when neither a global nor channel override is set; other channels default to 0. Zero disables ordinary burst batching, but Telegram still reassembles near-limit long-message chunks.

byChannel.title: Inbound Debounce by Channel (ms)
byChannel.description: Per-channel inbound debounce overrides keyed by provider id in milliseconds. Use this where some providers send message fragments more aggressively than others.

inbound.title: Inbound Debounce
inbound.description: Direct inbound debounce settings used before queue/turn processing starts. Configure this for provider-specific rapid message bursts from the same sender.

ackReaction.title: Ack Reaction Emoji
ackReaction.description: Emoji reaction used to acknowledge inbound messages (empty disables).

ackReactionScope.title: Ack Reaction Scope
ackReactionScope.description: When to send ack reactions ("group-mentions", "group-all", "direct", "all", "off", "none"). "group-mentions" acks group messages that mention the agent, whether or not the group requires mentions; "group-all" acks every group message. "off"/"none" disables ack reactions entirely.

enabled.title: Enable Status Reactions
enabled.description: Enable lifecycle status reactions on supported channels. Discord treats unset as enabled when ack reactions are active; Slack, Signal, Telegram, and WhatsApp require this to be true before lifecycle reactions are used. Slack uses native assistant thread status for progress by default.

statusReactions.title: Status Reactions
statusReactions.description: Lifecycle status reactions that update the emoji on the trigger message as the agent progresses (queued → thinking → tool → done/error).

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Message infrastructure and cross-agent defaults. Root siblings own infrastructure and cross-agent defaults; agents.defaults owns agent-loop behavior; agent entries may override either where supported.

persona.title: TTS Persona
persona.description: Default TTS persona id. Local TTS persona preferences can override this per host.

providers.title: TTS Persona Provider Bindings
providers.description: Provider-specific TTS persona bindings keyed by speech provider id. These merge over tts.providers for the active persona.

additionalProperties.title: TTS Persona
additionalProperties.description: One TTS persona. Use provider-specific bindings for exact voices/models and prompt templates.

personas.title: TTS Personas
personas.description: Named TTS personas that define stable spoken identity plus provider-specific speech bindings.

apiKey.title: TTS Provider API Key
apiKey.description: Provider API key used by that speech provider when its plugin requires authenticated TTS access.

additionalProperties.title: TTS Provider Config
additionalProperties.description: Provider-specific TTS configuration for one speech provider id. Keep fields scoped to the plugin that owns that provider.

providers.title: TTS Provider Settings
providers.description: Provider-specific TTS settings keyed by speech provider id. Use this instead of bundled provider-specific top-level keys so speech plugins stay decoupled from core config schema.

tts.title: Text-to-Speech
tts.description: Text-to-speech policy for reading agent replies aloud on supported voice or audio surfaces. Keep disabled unless voice playback is part of your operator/user workflow.

native.title: Native Commands
native.description: Registers native slash/menu commands with channels that support command registration (Discord, Slack, Telegram). Keep enabled for discoverability unless you intentionally run text-only command workflows.

nativeSkills.title: Native Skill Commands
nativeSkills.description: Registers native skill commands so users can invoke skills directly from provider command menus where supported. Keep aligned with your skill policy so exposed commands match what operators expect.

text.title: Text Commands
text.description: Enables text-command parsing in chat input in addition to native command surfaces where available. Keep this enabled for compatibility across channels that do not support native command registration.

bash.title: Allow Bash Chat Command
bash.description: Allow bash chat command (`!`; `/bash` alias) to run host shell commands (default: false; requires tools.elevated).

bashForegroundMs.title: Bash Foreground Window (ms)
bashForegroundMs.description: How long bash waits before backgrounding (default: 2000; 0 backgrounds immediately).

config.title: Allow /config
config.description: Allow /config chat command to read/write config on disk (default: false).

mcp.title: Allow /mcp
mcp.description: Allow /mcp chat command to manage OpenClaw MCP server config under mcp.servers (default: false).

plugins.title: Allow /plugins
plugins.description: Allow /plugins chat command to list discovered plugins and toggle plugin enablement in config (default: false).

debug.title: Allow /debug
debug.description: Allow /debug chat command for runtime-only overrides (default: false).

restart.title: Allow Restart
restart.description: Allow /restart, /update, and external SIGUSR2 restart requests (default: true).

ownerAllowFrom.title: Command Owners
ownerAllowFrom.description: Explicit owner allowlist for owner-scoped commands. Use channel-native IDs (optionally prefixed like "whatsapp:+15551234567"). '*' is ignored.

allowFrom.title: Command Elevated Access Rules
allowFrom.description: Defines elevated command allow rules by channel and sender for owner-level command surfaces. Use narrow provider-specific identities so privileged commands are not exposed to broad chat audiences.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description: Controls chat command surfaces, owner gating, and elevated command access behavior across providers. Keep defaults unless you need stricter operator controls or broader command availability.

enabled.title: Forward Exec Approvals
enabled.description: Enables forwarding of exec approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Keep disabled in low-risk setups and enable only when human approval responders need channel-visible prompts.

mode.title: Approval Forwarding Mode
mode.description: Controls where approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths. Use "session" as baseline and expand only when operational workflow requires redundancy.

agentFilter.title: Approval Agent Filter
agentFilter.description: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to limit forwarding blast radius and avoid notifying channels for unrelated agents.

sessionFilter.title: Approval Session Filter
sessionFilter.description: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded to shared destinations.

channel.title: Approval Target Channel
channel.description: Channel/provider ID used for forwarded approval delivery, such as discord, slack, or a plugin channel id. Use valid channel IDs only so approvals do not silently fail due to unknown routes.

to.title: Approval Target Destination
to.description: Destination identifier inside the target channel (channel ID, user ID, or thread root depending on provider). Verify semantics per provider because destination format differs across channel integrations.

accountId.title: Approval Target Account ID
accountId.description: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups when approvals must route through a specific account context. Use this only when the target channel has multiple configured identities.

threadId.title: Approval Target Thread ID
threadId.description: Optional thread/topic target for channels that support threaded delivery of forwarded approvals. Use this to keep approval traffic contained in operational threads instead of main channels.

targets.title: Approval Forwarding Targets
targets.description: Explicit delivery targets used when forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details. Keep target lists least-privilege and validate each destination before enabling broad forwarding.

exec.title: Exec Approval Forwarding
exec.description: Groups exec-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Configure here when approval prompts must reach operational channels instead of only the origin thread.

enabled.title: Forward Plugin Approvals
enabled.description: Enables forwarding of plugin approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Independent of approvals.exec.enabled.

mode.title: Plugin Approval Forwarding Mode
mode.description: Controls where plugin approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths.

agentFilter.title: Plugin Approval Agent Filter
agentFilter.description: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded plugin approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to limit forwarding blast radius.

sessionFilter.title: Plugin Approval Session Filter
sessionFilter.description: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded.

channel.title: Plugin Approval Target Channel
channel.description: Channel/provider ID used for forwarded plugin approval delivery, such as discord, slack, or a plugin channel id.

to.title: Plugin Approval Target Destination
to.description: Destination identifier inside the target channel (channel ID, user ID, or thread root depending on provider).

accountId.title: Plugin Approval Target Account ID
accountId.description: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups when plugin approvals must route through a specific account context.

threadId.title: Plugin Approval Target Thread ID
threadId.description: Optional thread/topic target for channels that support threaded delivery of forwarded plugin approvals.

targets.title: Plugin Approval Forwarding Targets
targets.description: Explicit delivery targets used when plugin approval forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details.

approvers.title: Default Slack Plugin Reviewers
approvers.description: Default Slack plugin reviewers as raw U/W user IDs within the selected Slack account, or workspace-qualified team:<team-id>:user:<user-id> values. Plugin and tool lists override this list for their own requests.

plugins.title: Slack Plugin Reviewer Overrides
plugins.description: Reviewer overrides keyed by the selected native tool plugin ID. Tool keys encode the raw tool name.

slack.title: Slack Plugin Reviewers
slack.description: Slack reviewer policy for plugin approvals. Omit the default approvers list to retain account allowFrom/defaultTo authorization; set it to [] to deny Slack decisions by default.

plugin.title: Plugin Approval Forwarding
plugin.description: Groups plugin-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Independent of exec approval forwarding. Configure here when plugin approval prompts must reach operational channels.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description: Approval routing controls for forwarding exec and plugin approval requests to chat destinations outside the originating session. Keep these disabled unless operators need explicit out-of-band approval visibility.

scope.title: Session Scope
scope.description: Sets base session grouping strategy: "per-sender" isolates by sender and "global" shares one session per channel context. Keep "per-sender" for safer multi-user behavior unless deliberate shared context is required.

dmScope.title: DM Session Scope
dmScope.description: DM session scoping: "main" keeps continuity, while "per-peer", "per-channel-peer", and "per-account-channel-peer" increase isolation. Use isolated modes for shared inboxes or multi-account deployments.

groupScope.title: Group Session Scope
groupScope.description: Group/channel session scoping: "per-group" keeps rooms separate while the agent main session ambiently watches them, independently of dmScope; "main" merges room context into main and needs no watch. Use "main" only for trusted rooms.

notifyOnCreate.title: Notify Home on Session Creation
notifyOnCreate.description: Queue a system notice in the owning agent's Home session when a session is created (default: true). Notices include available title and creator metadata and are read on the next Home turn or heartbeat. Set false to disable; drafts, incognito, internal sessions, and scheduled cron runs are excluded.

identityLinks.title: Session Identity Links
identityLinks.description: Maps canonical identities to provider-prefixed peer IDs so equivalent users resolve to one DM thread (example: telegram:123456). Use this when the same human appears across multiple channels or accounts.

resetTriggers.title: Session Reset Triggers
resetTriggers.description: Lists message triggers that force a session reset when matched in inbound content. Use sparingly for explicit reset phrases so context is not dropped unexpectedly during normal conversation.

mode.title: Session Reset Mode
mode.description: Selects reset strategy: "none" disables automatic reset (the default), "daily" resets at a configured hour, and "idle" resets after inactivity. /new and /reset remain available in every mode.

atHour.title: Session Daily Reset Hour
atHour.description: Sets local-hour boundary (0-23) for daily reset mode so sessions roll over at predictable times. Use with mode=daily and align to operator timezone expectations for human-readable behavior.

idleMinutes.title: Session Reset Idle Minutes
idleMinutes.description: Sets inactivity window before reset for idle mode and can also act as secondary guard with daily mode. Use larger values to preserve continuity or smaller values for fresher short-lived threads.

reset.title: Session Reset Policy
reset.description: Defines the default reset policy object used when no type-specific or channel-specific override applies. By default sessions do not reset automatically; use daily or idle schedules to opt in, while /new and /reset remain available at any time.

direct.title: Session Reset (Direct)
direct.description: Defines reset policy for direct chats and supersedes the base session.reset configuration for that type. Use this as the canonical direct-message override instead of the legacy dm alias.

group.title: Session Reset (Group)
group.description: Defines reset policy for group chat sessions where continuity and noise patterns differ from DMs. Use shorter idle windows for busy groups if context drift becomes a problem.

thread.title: Session Reset (Thread)
thread.description: Defines reset policy for thread-scoped sessions, including focused channel thread workflows. Use this when thread sessions should expire faster or slower than other chat types.

resetByType.title: Session Reset by Chat Type
resetByType.description: Overrides reset behavior by chat type (direct, group, thread) when defaults are not sufficient. Use this when group/thread traffic needs different reset cadence than direct messages.

resetByChannel.title: Session Reset by Channel
resetByChannel.description: Provides channel-specific reset overrides keyed by provider/channel id for fine-grained behavior control. Use this only when one channel needs exceptional reset behavior beyond type-level policies.

store.title: Session Store Path
store.description: Sets the session storage file path used to persist session records across restarts. Use an explicit path only when you need custom disk layout, backup routing, or mounted-volume storage.

mainKey.title: Session Main Key
mainKey.description: Accepted but ignored: the per-agent main session suffix is always "main". Omit this field; global session scope uses "global" instead.

default.title: Session Send Policy Default Action
default.description: Sets fallback action when no sendPolicy rule matches: "allow" or "deny". Keep "allow" for simpler setups, or choose "deny" when you require explicit allow rules for every destination.

action.title: Session Send Rule Action
action.description: Defines rule decision as "allow" or "deny" when the corresponding match criteria are satisfied. Use deny-first ordering when enforcing strict boundaries with explicit allow exceptions.

channel.title: Session Send Rule Channel
channel.description: Matches rule application to a specific channel/provider id (for example discord, telegram, slack). Use this when one channel should permit or deny delivery independently of others.

chatType.title: Session Send Rule Chat Type
chatType.description: Matches rule application to chat type (direct, group, thread) so behavior varies by conversation form. Use this when DM and group destinations require different safety boundaries.

keyPrefix.title: Session Send Rule Key Prefix
keyPrefix.description: Matches a normalized session-key prefix after internal key normalization steps in policy consumers. Use this for general prefix controls, and prefer rawKeyPrefix when exact full-key matching is required.

rawKeyPrefix.title: Session Send Rule Raw Key Prefix
rawKeyPrefix.description: Matches the raw, unnormalized session-key prefix for exact full-key policy targeting. Use this when normalized keyPrefix is too broad and you need agent-prefixed or transport-specific precision.

match.title: Session Send Rule Match
match.description: Defines optional rule match conditions that can combine channel, chatType, and key-prefix constraints. Keep matches narrow so policy intent stays readable and debugging remains straightforward.

rules.title: Session Send Policy Rules
rules.description: Ordered allow/deny rules evaluated before the default action, for example `{ action: "deny", match: { channel: "discord" } }`. Put most specific rules first so broad rules do not shadow exceptions.

sendPolicy.title: Session Send Policy
sendPolicy.description: Controls cross-session send permissions using allow/deny rules evaluated against channel, chatType, and key prefixes. Use this to fence where session tools can deliver messages in complex environments.

enabled.title: Thread Binding Enabled
enabled.description: Global master switch for thread-bound session spawning, routing, and delivery. Disable to turn off thread binding globally.

idleHours.title: Thread Binding Idle Timeout (hours)
idleHours.description: Default inactivity window in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables idle expiry). Default: 24.

maxAgeHours.title: Thread Binding Max Age (hours)
maxAgeHours.description: Optional hard max age in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables hard cap). Default: 0.

spawnSessions.title: Thread-Bound Session Spawns
spawnSessions.description: Global default gate for creating thread-bound work sessions from sessions_spawn and ACP thread spawns. Default: true when thread bindings are enabled.

defaultSpawnContext.title: Thread Spawn Context
defaultSpawnContext.description: Default native subagent context for thread-bound spawns. Use "fork" to start from the requester transcript or "isolated" for a clean child. Default: "fork".

threadBindings.title: Session Thread Bindings
threadBindings.description: Shared defaults for thread-bound session spawning and routing across supported channels. Configure global defaults here and override per channel only when behavior differs.

readOnly.title: Allow Read-only Sessions
readOnly.description: Allows sessions to be made read-only for non-participants. Default: true.

suggest.title: Allow Suggest Sessions
suggest.description: Allows suggest visibility. In this phase it enforces the same admission policy as read-only; suggestion queues are configured by a later feature. Default: true.

drafts.title: Allow Draft Sessions
drafts.description: Allows draft visibility, which hides sessions from non-owner, non-admin operators. Default: true.

sharing.title: Session Sharing Modes
sharing.description: Controls which collaboration modes session owners and administrators may select. Omitted booleans default to enabled; set a mode false to remove it from the picker and reject new selections.

mode.title: Session Maintenance Mode
mode.description: Determines whether pruning and disk-budget policies are only reported ("warn") or actively applied ("enforce"). Keep "warn" during rollout and switch to "enforce" after validating safe thresholds. Cold storage has its own explicit enabled setting.

enabled.title: Automatically Archive Old Transcripts
enabled.description: Enables background transcript archival (default false). A worker checks for eligible transcripts every minute. This explicit archive policy is separate from deletion and disk-budget cleanup.

afterDays.title: Archive After Inactive Days
afterDays.description: Archive transcripts after this many inactive days (positive integer, default 30). Active work is protected; changing the cutoff takes effect on the next worker pass without a Gateway restart.

coldStorage.title: Transcript Cold Storage
coldStorage.description: Moves inactive transcripts into compressed JSONL archives while retaining session metadata. Archive files become required history and must be included in backups. Changes apply without restarting the Gateway.

pruneAfter.title: Session Prune After
pruneAfter.description: Archives eligible durable conversations and removes disposable automation entries older than this duration (default `30d`; for example `12h`). Archived conversations retain their history and can be restored; protected or routable conversations remain active.

archiveDashboardAfter.title: Archive Inactive Dashboard Sessions After
archiveDashboardAfter.description: Archives inactive dashboard sessions after this duration (for example `7d`) so they remain available without crowding the active session list. Set `false` or `0` to disable automatic dashboard archiving.

maxEntries.title: Session Max Entries
maxEntries.description: Caps unarchived session entries (default 5000). Eligible durable overflow conversations are archived with their history; disposable automation entries are removed. Existing archives do not consume the cap. Protected active entries still count and can keep the store above the limit.

preserveRecent.title: Preserve Recent Sessions
preserveRecent.description: Protects interactive sessions active within this duration (for example `7d`) from automatic age, count, and disk-budget history eviction. Unset or `false` keeps the normal oldest-first policy. Synthetic model-run, cron, hook, heartbeat, ACP, and sub-agent rows remain eligible for bounded cleanup.

resetArchiveRetention.title: Session Reset Archive Retention
resetArchiveRetention.description: Age-based retention for archived transcripts (`*.reset.<timestamp>` and `*.deleted.<timestamp>`). Defaults to keeping archives until the disk budget evicts them oldest-first; set a duration (for example `30d`) to opt into wall-clock deletion, or `false` to disable it explicitly.

maxDiskBytes.title: Session Max Disk Budget
maxDiskBytes.description: Per-agent physical disk budget covering SQLite main/WAL and counted session-directory artifacts (for example `500mb`). Defaults to `10gb`; protected data can keep usage above the target. When exceeded, warn mode reports pressure and enforce mode removes old reset/delete artifacts, unreferenced history, then cap-created archives. Manual, age-retention, dashboard, recovery, and legacy archives remain protected. Set `false`, `0`, or `"0"` to disable.

highWaterBytes.title: Session Disk High-water Target
highWaterBytes.description: Target size after disk-budget cleanup (high-water mark). Defaults to 80% of maxDiskBytes; set explicitly for tighter reclaim behavior on constrained disks. A value that resolves to zero falls back to the default; negative values are invalid. Disable the budget with maxDiskBytes instead.

maintenance.title: Session Maintenance
maintenance.description: Automatic session-store maintenance controls for dashboard archiving, pruning age, entry caps, reset archive retention, and disk budget cleanup. Start in warn mode to observe impact, then enforce once thresholds are tuned.

session.title: Session
session.description: Global session routing, reset, delivery policy, and maintenance controls for conversation history behavior. Keep defaults unless you need stricter isolation, retention, or delivery constraints.

enabled.title: Automations Enabled
enabled.description: Enables automation execution for stored schedules managed by the gateway. Keep enabled for normal reminder/automation flows, and disable only to pause all automation execution without deleting jobs.

skipMissedJobs.title: Skip Missed Recurring Automations
skipMissedJobs.description: Skips missed recurring cron/every slots at Gateway startup and schedules their next future occurrence instead of catching up. Default: false. Enable to avoid stale reminders after downtime; one-shot at jobs still catch up.

webhookToken.title: Automations Webhook Bearer Token
webhookToken.description: Bearer token attached to automation webhook POST deliveries when webhook mode is used. Prefer secret/env substitution and rotate this token regularly if shared webhook endpoints are internet-reachable.

dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.title: Automations Webhook Dangerously Allow Private Network
dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.description: Allows automation webhooks to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless every configured webhook destination is trusted.

allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange.title: Automations Webhook Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange.description: Allows automation webhooks to RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange.title: Automations Webhook Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange.description: Allows automation webhooks to IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

allowedHostnames.title: Automations Webhook Allowed Hostnames
allowedHostnames.description: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for automation webhook delivery, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

blockedHostnames.title: Automations Webhook Blocked Hostnames
blockedHostnames.description: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules for automation webhook delivery. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

webhookSsrfPolicy.title: Automations Webhook SSRF Policy
webhookSsrfPolicy.description: SSRF policy applied to every outbound automation webhook. Private, loopback, link-local, and internal targets stay blocked unless this policy explicitly allows them. Keep unset for strict delivery.

sessionRetention.title: Automations Session Retention
sessionRetention.description: Controls how long completed automation run sessions are kept before pruning (`24h`, `7d`, `1h30m`, or `false` to disable pruning; a zero duration such as `0h` also disables; default: `24h`). Use shorter retention to reduce storage growth on high-frequency schedules.

cron.title: Automations
cron.description: Global scheduler settings for stored automations, run concurrency, delivery fallback, and run-session retention. Keep defaults unless you are scaling automation volume or integrating external webhook receivers.

enabled.title: Transcripts Enabled
enabled.description: Enables durable automatic meeting notes, the transcripts agent tool, and configured auto-start sources. Default: true. Set false to disable persistence and the tool; explicit meeting transcribe mode retains its bounded live tail.

providerId.title: Transcript Source Provider ID
providerId.description: Transcript source provider id, such as a Discord voice or future Slack huddle provider. Use the exact id exposed by the provider plugin.

whenOccupied.title: Transcript Capture When Occupied
whenOccupied.description: Start a fresh transcript session each time humans are present in the source and stop it (generating notes) after the last human leaves. Requires a provider that reports occupancy, such as discord-voice. Default: false (capture continuously from gateway start).

sessionId.title: Transcript Session ID
sessionId.description: Optional fixed transcript session id for this auto-start source. Ignored when whenOccupied is true. Leave unset for generated ids unless you need a stable daily selector and can avoid same-day collisions.

title.title: Transcript Title
title.description: Optional title for future transcript captures. Changing only titles keeps current captures running and does not rename their admitted title or saved notes. Other source changes retain their normal restart handling.

accountId.title: Transcript Account ID
accountId.description: Optional provider account or workspace identifier for transcript sources that need account disambiguation. Use the provider's documented account id format.

guildId.title: Discord Guild ID
guildId.description: Optional Discord guild id for Discord voice transcript sources. Configure this with the matching channelId when the provider needs guild-scoped voice channel lookup.

channelId.title: Transcript Channel ID
channelId.description: Provider channel id for the live transcript source, such as a Discord voice channel or Slack huddle channel. Verify provider-specific id semantics before enabling auto-start.

meetingUrl.title: Transcript Meeting URL
meetingUrl.description: Optional meeting URL for providers that join by URL instead of channel id. Use only trusted meeting links because auto-start may join and capture that meeting.

autoStart.title: Transcripts Auto-start Sources
autoStart.description: Live transcript sources managed automatically from gateway startup. Each entry is enabled by being present; remove an entry to disable that source. Sources capture continuously unless whenOccupied is enabled.

transcripts.title: Transcripts
transcripts.description: Core transcript capture settings for meeting notes, recording-capable agent tools, and configured live meeting auto-start sources. Meeting plugins capture durable notes by default; set enabled to false to opt out globally.

enabled.title: Hooks Enabled
enabled.description: Enables the hooks endpoint and mapping execution pipeline for inbound webhook requests. Keep disabled unless you are actively routing external events into the gateway.

path.title: Hooks Endpoint Path
path.description: HTTP path used by the hooks endpoint (for example `/hooks`) on the gateway control server. Use a non-guessable path and combine it with token validation for defense in depth.

token.title: Hooks Auth Token
token.description: Shared bearer token checked by hooks ingress for request authentication before mappings run. Treat holders as full-trust callers for the hook ingress surface, not as a separate non-owner role. Use environment substitution and rotate regularly when webhook endpoints are internet-accessible.

defaultSessionKey.title: Hooks Default Session Key
defaultSessionKey.description: Fallback session key used for hook deliveries when a request does not provide one through allowed channels. Use a stable but scoped key to avoid mixing unrelated automation conversations.

allowRequestSessionKey.title: Hooks Allow Request Session Key
allowRequestSessionKey.description: Allows callers to supply a session key in hook requests when true, enabling caller-controlled routing. Keep false unless trusted integrators explicitly need custom session threading.

allowedSessionKeyPrefixes.title: Hooks Allowed Session Key Prefixes
allowedSessionKeyPrefixes.description: Allowlist of accepted session-key prefixes for inbound hook requests when caller-provided keys are enabled. Use narrow prefixes to prevent arbitrary session-key injection.

allowedAgentIds.title: Hooks Allowed Agent IDs
